paper_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the three primary criteria for selecting an ideal polymer donor to be paired with non-fullerene acceptors in organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The three key criteria are: 1) possessing appropriate energy levels to ensure efficient exciton dissociation and high open-circuit voltage (Voc); 2) having complementary absorption spectra with the acceptor to maximize the short-circuit current (Jsc); and 3) maintaining morphological compatibility to achieve ideal phase separation and efficient charge transport.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the organic solar cell based on the PTFBDT-BZS donor and IDIC acceptor when optimized with 0.25% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO)?
qa_pairs.answer: The PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC-based device optimized with 0.25% DIO achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 11.03%, with an average PCE of 10.97% across 20 devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Why do wide-bandgap polymer donors like PDCBT, J51, PTFBDT-BZS, and PDBT-T1 show superior performance compared to the narrow-bandgap donor PTB7-Th when paired with the IDIC acceptor?
qa_pairs.answer: Wide-bandgap polymer donors outperform narrow-bandgap donors like PTB7-Th in IDIC-based systems because they offer better complementary absorption in the visible-NIR range. While the PTB7-Th:IDIC device only reached a PCE of 5.24%, the wide-bandgap donors achieved higher efficiencies ranging from 6.28% to 9.20% in as-cast devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the HOMO level of the polymer donor influence the open-circuit voltage (Voc) in IDIC-based solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The open-circuit voltage (Voc) is directly related to the HOMO levels of the polymer donors. Among the tested materials, PTFBDT-BZS has the deepest HOMO level, which resulted in the highest Voc of 0.921 V in the IDIC-based devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What morphological improvements occur in PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC and PDBT-T1:IDIC blends upon the addition of 0.25% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO)?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of 0.25% DIO improves molecular packing, increases domain purity, and optimizes phase separation. These morphological enhancements lead to higher fill factors (FF) and improved short-circuit current (Jsc) in the resulting solar cells.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: According to Resonant soft X-ray scattering (R-SoXS), what is the effect of 0.25% DIO on the domain purity of PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blended films?
qa_pairs.answer: R-SoXS analysis shows that the relative domain purity of the PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blended films increases from 0.74 in the as-cast state to 1.0 when 0.25% DIO is added as a solvent additive.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What does the relationship Jsc ∝ P^1.0 signify regarding the charge carrier dynamics in PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The linear relationship between short-circuit current (Jsc) and light intensity (P) indicates that virtually all free charge carriers are successfully swept out and collected at the electrodes before bimolecular recombination can occur.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIWAXS data, what is the predominant molecular orientation of PTFBDT-BZS:IDIC blends, and how does this affect device physics?
qa_pairs.answer: The blends exhibit a predominant 'face-on' molecular orientation, characterized by stronger π-π stacking in the out-of-plane direction compared to the in-plane direction. This orientation is beneficial for device performance as it facilitates efficient vertical charge transport between the electrodes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Mapping Polymer Donors toward High-Efficiency Fullerene Free Organic Solar Cells
